title: I INVITE YOU OVER A TEA
author: Bharadwaj Mishra
text:
I invite you over a tea,
but come with a song
that engulfs the table
that mahogany does
to the concrete jungle
with two ears on one side
of the rhythms and
one pair of lips that
do the music spread.

Come on the music
come over my teacup,

Between the lips and the cup
hang centuries of invitation.

Unfold the skin of Chitamruga
you said was hunted
by the Kaviraj’s father
I shall roll my Kasturi on its tuft
after you and roll in ecstasy
he would have had in 1914,
a birthday gift for his grandson
born that very morning.

I invite you over a tea,
and take a promise that you come
a little early next time
may be at 18 may be 21.
